prompt: A shop sells 3 notebooks at £2.40 each. You pay £10. What change should you receive? Explain briefly.
reference: 3 × 2.40 = 7.20; 10 − 7.20 = £2.80. Both arithmetic and final amount matter.
response_1: The notebooks cost 3 × £2.40 = £7.20. Your change is £10 − £7.20 = £2.80.
response_2: The notebooks cost £7.20, so your change from £10 is £3.80.

prompt: Explain overfitting in exactly two bullet points. Use simple language and mention unseen data.
reference: Overfitting fits training-specific details or noise and harms generalisation to unseen data. Require two bullet points, simple language and unseen data.

response_2:
• Overfitting means learning the training examples too closely, including noise.
• The model may then make poor predictions on unseen data.
